findings.title: Inbox lets the CEO approve a company-less legacy login inline, skipping the Workforce screen's company check
findings.scenario: GET /auth/staff/pending still returns legacy pending rows with tenantId null, from the removed self-signup, which let callers pick their own role, including legacy 'manager'. The inbox shows each one with a live Approve button. /workforce deliberately disables Approve on these rows (workforce/page.tsx ~l.975: `disabled={... || !user.tenantId}`, 'Tick a company and save before approving'). PATCH /auth/staff/:id/approve does not check this itself. Reproduced on servd_test_ceo_rv with a scratchpad probe: I seeded a pending user {role:'manager', tenantId:null}. The CEO's inbox item had approve with no disabledReason. Calling it returned 200, and the user became accountStatus 'active', tenantId null, role 'manager'. Result: an active, self-chosen-role staff login with no company, which the module's own screen never allows.
findings.fix: In the staffLogins provider, when r.tenantId is null, give the approve action `disabledReason: 'Pick a company for this login on Workforce first'` (or drop the inline approve and keep reject plus the /workforce link). Better still, also have PATCH /auth/staff/:id/approve refuse (422) a login with no tenantId, so no client can skip the check.

findings.title: HR requests in a multi-company HOD's other companies disappear from the inbox, while /hr/team still counts them
findings.scenario: A boh_management HOD belongs to companies A and B, with A active, and has one HR request waiting in each. Probe result: GET /hr/team pendingApprovals = 2, but GET /approvals/counts gives hr_request 1. Only 'All companies' view shows 2. The old 'My approvals' (/hr/approvals, now a redirect) listed every member company's requests on purpose ('the inbox spans every company'). So after the redirect, a head-office HOD no longer sees company B's request unless they switch view. Meanwhile /team's 'Waiting on you' stat and AppShell's personal-link condition (team.pendingApprovals) still report the full number, so the two counts disagree.
findings.fix: Either keep HR steps across the user's member companies (the HR resolver already limits them to memberTenantIds and the step owner), labelled by company, or keep the view scoping and make /hr/team pendingApprovals and the /team stat use the same view-scoped count. Then add a hint on the inbox when other companies hold items ('N more in other companies — switch to All companies').

findings.title: Stock-transfer deep link goes to /inventory, which has no transfer screen
findings.scenario: The stock_transfer provider sets link '/inventory'. With the Stock transfers chip selected, the inbox page shows 'Open stock transfers in its module →' pointing there. No admin page (and no tablet or mobile client) calls /stock-transfers, so the link opens a page with no transfers on it.
findings.fix: Set the type link to '/ceo/approvals?type=stock_transfer' (the page already hides the module link for /ceo/approvals links), or to null, until a transfer screen exists.

findings.title: Inbox company badge uses a hard-coded colour instead of a token
findings.scenario: In ItemCard, the company label background is `rgb(90 33 86 / 0.1)`, which is #5a2156 typed in by hand. CLAUDE.md says never hard-code a colour in a page and to use the admin tokens (--erp-secondary).
findings.fix: Use `color-mix(in srgb, var(--erp-secondary) 10%, transparent)`, or add an --erp-secondary-rgb token and use `rgb(var(--erp-secondary-rgb) / 0.1)`.
